_comment: How each confirmed town heats. Numbers: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2019-2023 5-year estimates, tables B25040 (house heating fuel, occupied homes), B25034 (year built) and B25024 (units in structure), pulled 2026-11-17. Gas company: Mass.gov 'Find my gas company' list (gas-2023.csv), pulled 2026-11-17. Percentages are rounded shares of occupied homes; oilHomes is the estimate itself. Update all rows together when a newer ACS release is used.

census.label: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2019-2023 (tables B25040, B25034, B25024)

gas.label: Mass.gov list of gas companies by town

lynn.note: Lynn has the most oil-heated homes of any North Shore town on Shane's list, about 6,800.

wakefield.utility: Wakefield Municipal Gas & Light Department (the state list also names National Grid)
wakefield.note: For gas on your street, ask Wakefield Municipal Gas & Light, 781-246-6363.

peabody.note: About 5,600 Peabody homes heat with oil, the second most on Shane's North Shore list after Lynn.

somerville.utility: National Grid or Eversource, depending on the street
somerville.note: Ask which company serves your street before planning an oil to gas switch.

boston.utility: National Grid or Eversource, depending on the neighborhood
boston.note: Ask which company serves your street before planning an oil to gas switch.

lexington.note: Lexington is in the state fossil-free building program, so National Grid asks Lexington customers to check with the town building department before requesting a gas connection; the program is aimed at new construction and major renovations.

notesSource.label: National Grid: Connect to natural gas (Lexington note)
